deepdive.sec: Cement & Building Materials — India Cements, now a 100%-brand-migrated UltraTech subsidiary

bull_bear.body: - Operating cash flows fully ploughed back into cement growth + dividends; "no requirement for further investment in cables & wires" for now. Dividend policy = percentage of profits ("expecting good dividends"). Net debt/EBITDA 0.87x, target < 1x. Growth funded by internal accruals.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **West Asia / fuel:** Strait of Hormuz shock, crude > USD 100; full cost hits Q2FY27; timing uncertain. Ocean-freight insurance up to 4–5%.
- **Monsoon/dry spells:** Rajasthan very dry (water-crisis demand risk *next* year); Q2 seasonal slowdown + kiln maintenance.
- **India Cements execution:** Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA + merger both hinge on capex flowing through by Q4FY28 — slippage watch.
- **Pricing:** monsoon-quarter prices expected "broadly steady"; cost pass-through of last 2 quarters still incomplete.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Very confident, delivery-focused, mildly immodest by design. Track record emphasised: crossed 200 MT a year early, completed India Cements/Kesoram brand migration a quarter early, and reaffirmed cables & wires for Q3FY27 — "we deliver what we commit." Candid on cost pressure and Q2 optics ("look through the noise"). India Cements framed explicitly as a promise-turned-trajectory (EBITDA/ton progression given quarter-by-quarter).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- India Cements' revenue *decline* is a reporting artefact (ex-factory switch), masking +21% like-for-like — a trap for a headline reader.
- The India Cements green-power leap **3% → 86% by FY28** is the single biggest, least-appreciated cost lever behind the Rs 603 → Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA path.
- UltraTech has *stopped reporting India Cements standalone volumes* — entire ICL volume now folded into UltraTech's number, signalling the merger endgame (Q4FY28).
- The Rs 1,400/ton UltraTech EBITDA "magical number" is explicitly pinned to Jan–Mar'28 "without any war" — a management-set, verifiable milestone.
- Coal has overtaken pet coke on energy economics → the fuel-mix shift to domestic coal is a margin tailwind if it holds.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet remains equity-heavy: shareholders' funds (including minority interest) of Rs 10,152 Cr against net debt of Rs 1,540 Cr as of June 2026.
- Net debt rose from Rs 1,271 Cr in March 2026 to Rs 1,540 Cr in June 2026, consistent with funding the approved capex partly through incremental borrowing.
- Net fixed assets including assets held for sale stand at Rs 11,913 Cr, but this includes Rs 5,303 Cr of revaluation reserves — reported asset base is not all cash-invested capital.
- Assets held for sale are carried on the books and exceptional items include impairment of investments/assets, pointing to ongoing portfolio pruning alongside reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **India Cements:** the turnaround centrepiece — EBITDA/ton Rs 603, brand migration 100% done, conversion ratio 1.5x, ~Rs 2,000 cr efficiency capex underway, green power headed 3%→86% by FY28. Merger into UltraTech standalone targeted Q4FY28.
- **Regional (UltraTech, this quarter):** East slowest (elections/labour); South & North a shade below 15%; West & Central above 15%. East seen inflecting structurally over next 2–4 years (land reforms, elections done).
- **Cables & Wires (new business):** facility complete, trial runs commenced, channel partners onboarding, regulatory approvals in place; launch Q3FY27; will "mature and milk" before any further capex.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Brand premium in a retail market:** UltraTech converted India Cements/Kesoram B/C-category customers to A-category willing to pay a premium — brand volume +21.3%; did not vacate the value space, migrated it up. Evidence: 76 operating facilities, ~2,000 warehouses, 150,000 channel partners, 477 RMC plants, 5,000+ UBS stores, ~50%+ dedicated transporters — a distribution/brand density "nobody else can come close to."
- **Secured raw material:** "every ton of committed expansion is fully backed by secured limestone" — no raw-material constraint on the growth path.
- **Cost buffers:** green power (47% of power at exit, cheaper), lead distance down to 360 km (from 367), clinker conversion 1.5x — structural cost advantages that let UltraTech "absorb the shock better than any peer and harvest relief faster."

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Presents itself as a subsidiary of UltraTech Cement Limited under a 'A Force For Good' banner, i.e. an integrated plant portfolio being folded into the market leader's operating and branding system.
- Asset base is South-India centric, with the deck naming four cement works: Sankar Nagar and Dalavoi and Sankari in Tamil Nadu and Malkapur in Telangana.
- A brand transition is underway and is already showing up as a structural reduction in marketing spend, indicating the company is selling under the parent's brand architecture rather than funding its own.
- Equity is listed on BSE and NSE with an additional overseas listing footprint (copy of the filing is circulated to the Luxembourg Stock Exchange).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Parentage] Control by UltraTech Cement is the central structural fact of the deck: the capex approval, brand transition and efficiency template all flow from the new parent.
- [Portfolio clean-up] Exceptional items relate to impairment of investment/asset and provisions for prior-period items, indicating legacy balance-sheet items are still being written down.
- [Disclosure scope] Financials are presented on a consolidated basis after elimination of inter-company transactions, and include JV/associate share of profit.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Held per-ton EBITDA essentially flat (> Rs 1,200) while growing absolute EBITDA +12% — "cost discipline + operating leverage as designed," on a base enlarged by still-ramping acquired assets.
- Cost headwinds: fuel +5% (Rs 874→915/ton), packing bags (Rs 9→~12/bag, the bigger Q1 hit), industrial diesel +~50% (Rs ~100→150s/litre) spiking limestone-raising cost (highest in 2 yrs). Pet coke now costlier than coal in energy terms → shift to domestic coal. Q2 cost +Rs 130–140/ton sequentially, then H2 relief hoped as war/freight normalise (ocean-freight insurance 1% → 4–5%).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** India Cements EBITDA/ton Rs 603 (from Rs 509 in Q4FY26; unbroken Rs 386→400→509→603 since Q2FY26); revenue +21% l-f-l (Rs 993 cr ex-factory), volume +19%; brand migration 100% complete; conversion ratio 1.5x. Guidance reaffirmed: Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA by Q4FY28, green power 3%→86% by FY28, ~Rs 2,000 cr efficiency capex, merger by Q4FY28. Parent UltraTech record Q1: volume +13.1%, EBITDA Rs 5,146 cr (+12%), PAT Rs 2,604 cr (+17.2%), EBITDA/ton > Rs 1,200, net debt/EBITDA 0.87x; capacity 205.5 MT → 212.7 MT (FY27) → 235 MT (Mar'28); Cables & Wires launch Q3FY27 (Rs 1,800 cr, Rs 888 cr spent). Q2FY27 cost +Rs 130–140/ton flagged.
- _next Q → check: India Cements EBITDA/ton progression toward Rs 1,000; green-power ramp; Q2 cost print (Rs 130–140/ton) vs actual; Cables & Wires commissioning (Q3FY27); merger milestones; UltraTech volume vs double-digit guide + industry growth._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
**India Cements-specific (logged as INDIACEM commitments):**
- **EBITDA Rs 1,000/ton "very much in sight" by Q4FY28** — with full benefit of the capex programme flowing through the P&L.
- **Green power 3% → ~86%** of India Cements' power requirement by end of FY28.
- **Cost-improvement capex ~Rs 2,000 cr** being deployed (waste-heat recovery, preheater upgradation, cooler upgradation).
- **ICL integration/merger to complete by Q4FY28** (or a quarter earlier) — pending capex completion + non-core land (asset) disposal + bringing operating parameters in line with UltraTech standalone.
- Q2FY27 to look "optically softer" (seasonal monsoon + West Asia cost weigh).

**Parent UltraTech (context — belongs under ULTRACEMCO, not logged here):**
- Double-digit domestic grey volume growth targeted for FY27; industry Q1 volume ~7–8%.
- Q2FY27 cost +Rs 130–140/ton sequentially (fuel + kiln maintenance + operating deleverage).
- Capacity: 205.5 MT total now → grey 212.7 MT by FY27-end → ~235 MT (India) by Mar'28; consolidated > 242 MT; capex ~Rs 17,000 cr over 2–2.5 yrs (all internal accruals).
- Green power 1,897 MW (47% of power at quarter exit) → 2.5–3 GW "very shortly."
- **Cables & Wires: commissioning + product launch reaffirmed for Q3FY27 (Oct–Dec'26)**; Rs 1,800 cr programme, Rs 888 cr spent/committed; aluminium from Hindalco (4-hr lead).
- UltraTech Rs 1,400/ton EBITDA target: Jan–Mar'28 quarter "without any war."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: - Not an order-book business. Demand pipeline framed as very rich: cement-intensive projects called out — Maharashtra Rs 20,000 cr shipbuilding cluster (Mazagaon Dock), Odisha Rs 50,000 cr+ deep seaport/shipbuilding (Ganjam/Paradip), Tamil Nadu ~Rs 18,000 cr data-centre/shipbuilding MoU, Ahmedabad-Dholera semi-HSR (~Rs 20,000 cr), Rs 30,000 cr NIIF infusion, Vadhavan port (packages awarded), Ken-Betwa river-linking. Housing/urban real estate = ~55–60% of consumption, strong start to CY26 (Mumbai registrations +6%).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- Cables & Wires the new growth engine (Q3FY27 launch); "sky is the limit" but no guidance — "profitable, grounded, grow with the market."
- Premiumization + blended-cement mix compounding blended realisations regardless of headline price. RMC only ~3.5% of UltraTech sales (retail 65–66%, institutional ~35%) → India remains a *branded* cement market (analogous to branded steel/paints) as long as it's an individual-homebuilder/retail market.
- Beyond 240 MT: team already "on the drawing board"; inorganic opportunities to be examined.

open.item: With prices improving in South markets from April, India Cements performance will improve further.

Fuel costs rose slightly to INR1.8/kCal this quarter; India Cements EBITDA dampened by shutdowns/maintenance and Tamil Nadu limestone royalty, though management expects ~INR100/ton of maintenance cost to reverse in Q3.
Management expects South India pricing to stabilize with upward bias driven by large institutional demand (Amravati, data centers, IT); calls FY26 a "fabulous year."
Management asserts India Cements will be a strong company at par with modern plants within 2-3 years driven by cost-cutting on pyro-processing, limestone, heat generation and coolers.
West Asia conflict flagged as a real near-term headwind on fuel, packing bags (up ~INR6/bag) and freight; UltraTech says price increases already taken in April are expected to offset the cost impact.
India Cements brand conversion crossed 58% at end of December '25 (Kesoram 69%); both to complete brand transition by June '26.
India Cements brand transition at 31% complete (Sept '25), to cross 40% by December quarter; both acquired brands (ICL & Kesoram) to complete transition not later than June '26.
Group expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum and targets double-digit growth for FY27; industry demand grew ~6-7% in Q4FY26 (~6.5% full year FY26).
India Cements cost-improvement capex committed INR601 crore, of which INR144 crore spent so far; benefits to start reflecting in the P&L from January-March '27.
India Cements EBITDA per ton (INR400 in Q3) targeted to reach INR1,000 exit by Q4FY27, driven by brand conversion, price hikes and the efficiency capex program.
India Cements + Kesoram brand transition to UltraTech to be completed (100%) before the end of fiscal '27.

India Cements capex plan of ~INR1,500 crore (INR1,000 crore towards WHRS and profit-improvement) with payback <3 years, to be spent in FY26 and FY27; benefits reflecting from the Jan-March '27 quarter.

Group-wide cost/efficiency improvement of upwards of INR300 per ton to be delivered over the 3-year window by FY27 (INR86/ton already delivered by FY25); India Cements/Kesoram efficiency programs run in parallel.
India Cements brand to be fully transitioned into UltraTech (via tolling + rebranding) by end of fiscal '27.
WHRS additions from acquired assets: ~22 MW for India Cements (ICL) plus ~24 MW for Kesoram, to be added to the network by FY27.
